question: Does sensor-channel permutation-invariant temporal recognition transfer when the same observed four-channel sequence arrives in unseen channel order, rather than exploiting a privileged channel zero?
hypothesis: A symmetric four-channel transition score may outperform a first-channel scorer under an unseen global permutation of the four channels without adding learned parameters.
source: Reuse frozen nonlinear 16x4 W-R18 sequence, 9 entities/seed. Original 4 channel readings receive +17 candidate offset and genuine modulo3 per-tick jitter in development, +61 and modulo5 jitter in heldout; negatives rearrange candidate rows preserving the first anchor and multiset. Both a and b sequences have channels permuted by the heldout-only permutation indices [1,2,3,0], so ground-truth order is unchanged by reindexing.
development_negative: Reverse 15 tail ticks for even entity; rotate tail left3 for odd entity.
heldout_negative: Unseen double adjacent row swaps at ticks5/6 and 10/11.
arms: unordered first-channel anchor-relative histogram score, one train-only scalar threshold
first-channel mean 15 circular transition mismatch, scalar threshold
channel-symmetric MAX of four per-channel mean transition mismatch scores, scalar threshold
channel-symmetric MEAN of four per-channel mean transition mismatch scores, scalar threshold
learning: For each arm threshold=midpoint(max development-positive score,min development-negative score); 72 same development examples, one scalar learned, no heldout tuning. Four-channel arms evaluate 4x sensor edges but no extra persistent learned parameters; compute cost explicitly increased.
primary: Four heldout seeds with TP,TN,FP,FN each; ROLE_TRANSFER if either symmetric arm accuracy>=0.85 and exceeds first-channel baseline strictly, with unordered<=0.55; PARTIAL if it beats baseline without meeting criterion; NEGATIVE otherwise. Keep all failures.
controls: Different development and heldout seed cohorts, identical candidate multiset in positive vs negative, genuine varying jitter, exact channel permutation both inputs, all 16-tick input lengths, no post-result threshold tuning, no first-use replay, original artifact and one full regression.
claim_limit: Synthetic sensor-channel symmetry, not semantic role binding in natural language or real-world general intelligence.
